text:
support_ella: FYI customer Acme reports p95/p99 spike since ~2026-03-16 04:00 UTC, many requests hitting 500s and a few GPU OOMs. attaching sample request ids and logs.

oncall_alice: Thanks, Ella. Any correlation with deploys or config changes?

support_ella: No deploys on their tenant; last config change was 3 days ago. they say latencies jumped suddenly around 04:00 UTC. sample req: req=acme-9876, model=redwood-small-q4_0, route=chat.generate

eng_runtime_bob: Can you paste the sample stack/logs? Also which cluster/zone?

support_ella: Logs for req acme-9876: ```
2026-03-16T04:01:02Z ERROR serve: request failed id=acme-9876 code=500 msg="out of memory" gpu=0 node=rt-34
2026-03-16T04:01:02Z WARN runtime: kv-cache growth: tenant=acme size_mb=1432 event=alloc
2026-03-16T04:01:02Z INFO slab: fragmentation_pct=78 free_mb=120 total_mb=1536
``` cluster=us-west-2a

eng_sre_mike: That fragmentation number is high. Looks like repeated KV allocations without eviction. Do we have the per-tenant KV cap enabled for this cluster?

eng_runtime_bob: Checking. infra metrics show KV growth on rt-34 around 03:55 UTC with several large bursts. I see a previously silent tenant-side workload (batch inference) that started pinging prefixes.

infra_bot: Alert triggered: GPU memory fragmentation > 70% on rt-3x pool (p95 latency + OOMs) at 2026-03-16T03:58:44Z.

oncall_alice: Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle the tenant's requests via rate limit 2) restart affected workers to reclaim fragments 3) enable eviction on KV cache for that tenant. Can support apply a soft throttle while eng takes a look?

support_ella: I asked Acme to pause their heavy batch job; they agreed to throttle by 10x for 30m. Applied temporary tenant throttle rule id=tmp-throttle-4101.

eng_runtime_bob: Good. On infra side I'll spin a rolling restart of the 3 pods on rt-34 with allocator tuning flag --slab-defrag=aggressive. Command: ```kubectl rollout restart deploy/rt-pool-34 -n runtime --grace-period=30```

eng_sre_mike: Before restart, let's do a graceful eviction pass to free prefix cache for acme: ```curl -X POST "https://internal-api/kv/evict" -d '{"tenant":"acme","policy":"LRU","target_mb":200}'``` That should reduce immediate memory pressure without full restarts.

eng_runtime_bob: Ran eviction at 4101240500, response: {"evicted_mb":118, "buckets":4}. Fragmentation dropped to 54% in ~90s.

support_manager_carol: Thanks. Any customer-facing mitigation we should offer beyond kept throttling and status updates? credits?

non-bot-note: deploy-bot: canary deploy of kv-cap patch scheduled at 4101242000 to cap per-tenant KV growth.

eng_sre_mike: Patch details: add config param tenant_kv_max_mb default=2048 and enforcement path in runtime allocator. Also adding metrics: tenant_kv_headroom_mb and eviction_triggers.

eng_runtime_bob: Plan: 1) keep throttle on Acme until canary lands 2) after canary, enable cap for acme tenant in canary config 3) observe p95/p99 and memory metrics 4) roll to rest of cluster if stable.

support_ella: Acme confirms latency improved to near baseline after throttle + eviction; still watching p99 tails. They asked for ETA on a permanent fix.

eng_sre_mike: ETA for canary is ~20m. If canary shows stable memory and p99 < pre-regression, we'll tag release and schedule full rollout tonight during low traffic window.

non-bot-note: infra_bot: canary start at 4101242000, target pods=5.

support_manager_carol: I'll prepare a short customer note: explain root cause (KV growth + fragmentation leading to occasional OOMs), immediate mitigations we did, and next steps (cap + rollout, allocator tuning). Offer 1 day of service credit.

eng_runtime_bob: Follow-ups for postmortem: - add automated eviction when tenant_kv_mb > 75% of slab headroom - surface tenant_kv_percent in console - add auto-throttle suggestion when shard OOM rate > threshold

support_ella: Posting summary to customer channel and will update ticket with timeline and credit offer. Thanks team. :thumbsup:"
